sections.h2: What are your options for selling a house in Davie, FL?
sections.html:
A Davie homeowner can list with an agent, sell privately, or accept a cash purchase of the house as it stands. The right route depends on how much repair work the house needs and how soon you need the proceeds.

Davie is a town in Broward County, and it behaves differently from the beach cities to the east. Its own history is tied to ranching, citrus and horses. If your lot has a barn, fencing, a pool or other outbuildings, those extras shape what an inspector will flag, so plan for them from the start.

  • Listing: the most exposure, with showings, an appraisal and a financing contingency.
  • Private sale: you handle the contract, disclosures and closing coordination.
  • Cash sale: a purchase with no lender, often used for inherited, tenant-occupied or repair-heavy homes.

sections.h2: What is the history behind Davie, FL?
sections.html:
Davie was incorporated on November 16, 1925, and the town marked its centennial with events from November 2024 through 2025. Early in the twentieth century it was known as Zona, settled by workers who were draining the Everglades, and it took its present name in 1916 from the developer R.P. Davie.

Agriculture shaped it from there. The Town describes Davie as a ranching and western-lifestyle community with horse trails, an annual rodeo and a western-themed downtown. The Old Davie School Historical Museum, built in 1918, is the oldest permanent school building in Broward County, and the Orange Blossom Festival began in 1937 to honor the local citrus industry.

For a seller, that heritage shows up in the rules and the buyer pool. The Town publishes a Western Theme Design Manual meant to preserve citrus, cattle, equestrian and rodeo heritage, so ask the Town whether it affects exterior changes on your parcel, especially in the western-themed district.

sections.h2: How big is Davie and who lives there?
sections.html:
The Town of Davie says it is home to more than 107,000 residents, and it describes a rural atmosphere, a western-themed district and a large educational complex as the traits that set it apart from other Broward municipalities.

Two sellers on opposite sides of town can face very different sales. A home on a half-acre lot with an equestrian setup is priced and marketed differently from a townhome in a planned community. Roof age, pool condition and any outbuildings are worth sorting out before showings.

If your property is in an association, request the governing documents early. Resale in many communities depends on association approval, estoppel letters and any pending special assessments, and a delay there can hold up a closing more than any repair.

sections.h2: Can you rent out a Davie house as a vacation rental instead?
sections.html:
Yes, but Davie regulates it through a registration program. Under the Town Code (Chapter 16, Article IX) and section 509.242 of the Florida Statutes, a vacation rental is a unit rented to transient guests more than three times in a calendar year for periods under thirty days, or one that is advertised as regularly rented that way.

The Town requires a license from the state Department of Business and Professional Regulation before it will accept the application. The packet also asks for proof of ownership from the Broward County Property Appraiser, corporate documents if an entity owns the home, interior and exterior sketches, a Department of Revenue registration and a Broward tourist tax number.

sections.h2: What do Broward County property taxes mean for a Davie seller?
sections.html:
Broward County values and bills your Davie property, and Florida's calendar controls the dates. Assessment is as of January 1, the proposed-tax notice arrives in August, and bills go out in November.

  • Exemption and classification applications are due March 1, which matters if your lot has an agricultural classification.
  • A petition against your value is filed with the clerk within 25 days of the proposed-tax notice.
  • Early payment earns 4 percent off in November, falling to 1 percent in February.
  • Taxes are delinquent after April 1.

Non-homestead assessed value can rise by no more than 10 percent a year, according to the state. Homestead property has the separate Save Our Homes cap, which is the lower of 3 percent or the change in the consumer price index. When the house sells, that protection ends and the buyer starts at just value.

If you ever received an agricultural classification on part of the land, ask the property appraiser what a sale or a change in use does to it before you sign a contract.

sections.h2: What does it cost to transfer the deed in Davie?
sections.html:
The deed is recorded with the Broward County clerk, and the state documentary stamp tax is 70 cents on each $100 of consideration. Consideration includes any mortgage or encumbrance on the property, whether or not the buyer assumes it, which is why a payoff does not shrink the base the way sellers sometimes expect.

The Department of Revenue says all parties to the document share liability for the tax regardless of who agrees to pay it. The contract assigns the cost, and the title company normally collects it at closing.

A recording fee applies on top of the tax. Section 28.24 sets the first page at $5.00 and each additional page at $4.00, with extra per-page charges for the records trust fund and technology. If a spouse is signing off on a homestead or a divorce deed is involved, the state lists specific exemptions, so ask the title agent before assuming the tax applies.

sections.h2: What if your Davie house is inherited, in foreclosure or has tenants?
sections.html:
Each situation has a defined path in Florida law, and a sale is still possible in all of them.

For an inherited home, a personal representative's deed under a probated will is not subject to documentary stamp tax according to the Department of Revenue. Estate planning transfers generally are taxable, though, because the Department states there is no specific exemption for them. Florida no longer collects an estate tax for people who died after December 31, 2004.

In foreclosure, the court's final judgment sets a sale date between 20 and 35 days out unless the plaintiff agrees to a longer wait. A buyer who closes first can pay the lender and leave the owner with any remaining equity.

With a tenant, nonpayment requires three days' written notice, weekends and court holidays excluded. A tenant who raises a defense other than payment must put the rent into the court registry within five days or lose those defenses.

faqs.q: Does Davie require registration for short-term rentals?
faqs.a: Yes. The Town runs a vacation rental registration program tied to Chapter 16, Article IX of its code, and it asks for a state DBPR license first. Contact the Police Code Compliance Division at 954-693-8237 before advertising.

faqs.q: What is the Davie vacation rental fee?
faqs.a: The Town lists $500 for a full registration year and $300 for the half year starting April 1. Renewals are $450 for a non-owner-occupied home and $400 for an owner-occupied one.

faqs.q: Who records a deed for a Davie property?
faqs.a: The Broward County clerk records it and collects the documentary stamp tax of 70 cents per $100. The title company normally arranges both at closing.

faqs.q: What happens to my property tax benefit when I sell in Davie?
faqs.a: The Save Our Homes cap ends with the sale, and the buyer is assessed at just value the next January 1. Ask the Broward property appraiser about portability if you are buying another Florida homestead.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Davie house with tenants still living there?
faqs.a: Yes. A buyer can take the house with the lease in place. If you want it vacant, month-to-month tenancies end with at least 30 days' notice under Florida law, and only a sheriff can carry out a removal.
